title: Measurements
intro: meas (and the netlist form .meas) pulls numbers out of results: delays, rise times, crossings, peaks, averages, rms values, integrals, derivatives, and expressions of other measurements. It works on dc, ac, tran and sp (spectrum) results, and each result becomes a vector you can compute with.

items: Trigger and target: meas tran tpd trig v(in) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 fall=1. The time from the trigger crossing to the target crossing. trig at=1n uses a fixed time instead of a crossing.
When: meas tran t1 when v(out)=0.9 cross=2 gives the time (frequency, swept value) at which the condition is met; when v(a)=v(b) for two signals crossing.
Find when / find at: meas tran v1 find v(x) when v(y)=0.5 fall=1; meas ac g1k find vdb(out) at=1k.
Statistics over a range: avg, min, max, pp (peak to peak), rms, min_at and max_at (where the extreme is), with from= and to=.
integ (integral) over a range: charge from a current, energy from power.

deriv at=... or deriv when ...: a slope. In ngspice 47 this form fails (meas says deriv is not supported, and .meas fails too); take let d = deriv(v(out)) and meas ... find d at=... instead, as in the sample.

param='expression': combine earlier results (.meas tran ratio param='tr/tf'). This works in .meas lines in the netlist; the meas command in a .control block rejects it in version 47, but there let ratio = tr/tf does the same, since results are vectors.
find par('expression') at=...: an expression of vectors at a point.

blocks.text: Crossing selectors: rise=N, fall=N, cross=N (either direction) and rise=last, fall=last, cross=last. td=delay ignores everything before that time (or swept value). For ac, at= and from/to are frequencies; for dc they are the swept value.

blocks.source:
A catalogue of measurements on an RC-loaded inverter-like waveform
VIN in 0 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 50p 50p 5n 10n)
R1 in out 2k
C1 out 0 1p
.control
  tran 5p 30n
  meas tran tpd   trig v(in) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0.9 rise=1
  meas tran trise trig v(out) val=0.18 rise=2 targ v(out) val=1.62 rise=2
  meas tran tfall trig v(out) val=1.62 fall=1 targ v(out) val=0.18 fall=1
  meas tran t_last when v(out)=0.9 cross=last
  meas tran vmid  find v(out) at=2n
  meas tran vx    find v(out) when v(in)=0.9 fall=2
  meas tran vavg  avg v(out) from=10n to=30n
  meas tran vrms  rms v(out) from=10n to=30n
  meas tran vpp   pp  v(out) from=10n to=30n
  meas tran tmax  max_at v(out) from=10n to=20n
  meas tran q     integ i(VIN) from=10n to=15n
  let dvdt = deriv(v(out))
  meas tran slope find dvdt at=11.5n
  let ratio = trise/tfall
  let tau = 2k*1p
  print tau ratio
.endc
.end

blocks.text: The RC time constant is 2 ns, so the 10 to 90% rise and fall times come out at 2.2 RC = 4.39 ns, and the 50% delay at ln 2 RC = 1.39 ns. The waveform does not settle fully in 5 ns, so it swings between about 0.14 and 1.66 V (pp = 1.52 V) and averages 0.91 V. q integrates the source current over the high half-cycle: -1.34 pC, the charge delivered into C (1 pF times the 1.34 V it gains in that half-cycle); negative because i(VIN) is measured into the source's + node.
meas in the control language and .meas in the netlist

items: .meas lines run automatically after the matching analysis in batch and interactive runs, and print their results. In batch mode with -r (output straight to a rawfile) the data are not kept in memory and .meas cannot run; use a .control block or .print lines.

meas commands in a .control block run on the current plot when the script reaches them; their results are vectors in that plot, and since version 45 the command accepts expressions (meas tran x find v(a)*v(b) at=1n).
A measurement that fails (the condition is never met) prints an error and creates no vector; scripts that use the result should check with if or let with a default.
Precision: set measureprec=N (version 46) or NGSPICE_MEAS_PRECISION for more printed digits; the vector itself is full precision.
.option autostop ends a transient as soon as all .meas lines have their answers.
meas does not work on noise plots (noise1, noise2); index the vectors there. In ngspice 47 it also crashes on the plot of an sp (S-parameter) run.

blocks.title: Duty cycle
blocks.text: Measure the duty cycle of a clock v(clk) with 0 to 1.2 V swing in its 5th period.
solution:
meas tran thigh trig v(clk) val=0.6 rise=5 targ v(clk) val=0.6 fall=5
meas tran tper trig v(clk) val=0.6 rise=5 targ v(clk) val=0.6 rise=6
meas tran duty param='thigh/tper'
(If the clock starts high, the 5th fall comes before the 5th rise; pick fall=6 in that case.)
blocks.answer: Two trig/targ measurements and a param ratio.

items: H. Vogt, G. Atkinson, D. Warning and P. Nenzi, Ngspice User's Manual, version 47, 2026 (ngspice.sourceforge.io/docs.html), section 11.4 (.meas) and 13.5 (meas command).
